description:
13 sites in src/memory.rs construct MemoryError from a serde_json::Error (or other Display source) using bare .to_string(), losing the operation context that the canonical sibling preserves:

src/memory.rs sites (count: 13):
  Line 248: MemoryError(e.to_string()) — get_objects, list path, to_value
  Line 250: MemoryError(e.to_string()) — get_objects, list path, from_value
  Line 261: MemoryError(e.to_string()) — get_objects, by-ids path, to_value
  Line 263: MemoryError(e.to_string()) — get_objects, by-ids path, from_value
  Line 461: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — create_object, to_value(obj)
  Line 464: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — create_object, from_value(node)
  Line 479: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — create_object, to_value(result)
  Line 481: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — create_object, from_value(result)
  Line 507: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — update_object, to_value(patch)
  Line 523: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — update_object, to_value(stored)
  Line 532: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — update_object, from_value(merged)
  Line 538: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — update_object, to_value(result)
  Line 540: BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(e.to_string())) — update_object, from_value(result)

What is wrong: when a downstream caller sees 'memory backend error: missing field name at line 1 column 23' as the wire response, they have no idea WHICH of the 13 round-trips failed. The error_type strings 'create_object, to_value(obj)' vs 'update_object, from_value(merged)' would localize the bug instantly.

Canonical comparison — jmap-mail-server src/memory.rs uses contextualized form everywhere:

  Line 500:  MemoryError(format!("deserialize {}: {e}", O::TYPE_NAME))
  Line 510:  MemoryError(format!("deserialize {}: {e}", O::TYPE_NAME))
  Line 544:  MemoryError(format!("invalid state token: {since_state}"))
  Line 963:  MemoryError(format!("serialize: {e}"))
  Line 1011: MemoryError(format!("deserialize after create: {e}"))
  Line 1223: MemoryError(format!("serialize email: {e}"))
  Line 1388: MemoryError(format!("blob not found: {blob_id}"))
  Line 1470: MemoryError(format!("deserialize source email: {e}"))
  Line 1510: MemoryError(format!("serialize copied email: {e}"))

Total: zero MemoryError(e.to_string()) sites in mail-server (except one solitary case at line 1045 which is also a divergence). The contextualized form IS the canonical idiom in this workspace.

What idiomatic Rust would do, in order of effort:

(a) Replace each site with a context-bearing format!:
    .map_err(|e| BackendSetError::Other(MemoryError(format!("create_object: to_value: {e}"))))?

(b) Add a helper:
    impl MemoryError {
        fn ctx<E: std::fmt::Display>(op: &'static str) -> impl FnOnce(E) -> Self {
            move |e| MemoryError(format!("{op}: {e}"))
        }
    }
    ...
    .map_err(MemoryError::ctx("create_object: to_value"))?

The .to_string() pattern in filenode-server is also tied to the existing finding JMAP-510h.37 (MemoryError::Display interpolates raw inner string — security contract violation): once the inner string carries 'description: "PASSWORD123" — invalid character at line 1 column 14', any logged error leaks the offending content. The context-prefix form does not eliminate that, but it makes it easier to scrub specific sites without scrubbing all of them.

Canonical-template rule: this is a regression from canonical, so the fix is in this crate alone. Mail-server already has the right pattern. No propagation needed.
title: MemoryError(e.to_string()) drops operation context — canonical mail-server uses MemoryError(format!("op: {e}"))
